comparison.objective: Candidate adjusts a gripper stop screw, locks its concentric jam nut without shifting the setting, then cycles the gripper; PR-236 supports a gravity-loaded inspection arm at an angle and engages a separate indexed clamp knob.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate requires simultaneous hex-driver and thin-wrench seating with countertorque against screw rotation caused by tightening its concentric nut; PR-236 instead supports an arm against gravity while turning a spatially separate knob whose reduced-order model supplies no lock reaction to the knob.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires a locked 90° setting retained within 3°, ≤2° drift over three released cycles, retained nuts, and 30 mm tool clearance; PR-236 requires the +15° arm aim, indexed lock engagement, and a two-second released hold within 3°/2° drift.
comparison.reason: The essential tested causality differs: preserving a threaded adjustment against concentric locknut reaction is not subsumed by holding a payload against gravity while actuating a separate indexed lock, although both share generic set-lock-release primitives.

review_notes.purpose: ONE bounded source-enhanced review. Prior comparison used only PR body; catalog had no task specs. Preserve original overlap and do not repeatedly resample this record. If overlap remains, reject this candidate.
review_notes.source_facts: Original README Indexed lock gives an eccentric vertical knob driving an axial pushrod/rosette on a horizontal arm hinge. The held arm opposes a pre-existing gravity torque; knob tightens a toothed lock at nearest5deg tooth. The source explicitly notes no tooth/spring reaction fed into knob; retain its intended physical force path rather than dismissing it for a reduced-order solver. It does NOT have two concentric threaded adjustment elements whose fastening rotates the adjusted screw.
review_notes.question: Determine whether that difference in essential physical causality constitutes a meaningfully different ability: current candidate proposes maintaining screw angular phase against reaction torque from turning its concentric nut, with two genuinely seated tools and real coupling. Generic set-angle/hold/tighten/release alone is not proof either way. Do not accept hardware names, a different target, cycles, tool count alone, or increased difficulty as novelty. If current gripper later lacks the proposed coupling, final novelty must fail. Retain overlap/uncertain if original ability still subsumes it.
